rationale.conceptual: DFT with spin–orbit coupling is an established method, but computing a reliable MAE for a large slab (≥60 Pt atoms) requires careful setup of pseudopotentials, exchange‑correlation functional, slab thickness, k‑point convergence, and a proper total‑energy difference scheme; several non‑trivial components must interact correctly to get the sign reversal reported in the paper.
rationale.execution: The pipeline requires (i) building slab/supercell models for two sites, (ii) preparing DFT input files for out‑of‑plane and in‑plane magnetization directions, (iii) running multiple SCF calculations and possibly additional convergence checks, (iv) extracting total energies, and (v) a final post‑processing script. This multi‑step orchestration involves installing and configuring a complex DFT package and managing several interdependent jobs.
